subsystem: Bench: how jev-on is measured and what it scored (src/bench/*, bench/results/*, docs/DESIGN.md §13, docs/STATUS.md live sections, ~/.jevcode/runs transcripts)
summary: The bench (src/bench/runner.ts) runs every condition of a task as a unit through the in-process engine, copies RunResult fields verbatim into tasks.jsonl, and aggregates with src/bench/metrics.ts (pass = passed/evaluated; paired tables over the intersection of evaluated tasks). Conditions are a closed union: EngineMode 'jev-on'|'jev-off'|'jev-only' (src/core/types.ts:371), mirrored in CONDITION_ORDER (src/bench/conditions.ts:12), CONDITIONS (src/cli/args.ts:277, validated :644-647), createEngineFor (conditions.ts:114-116: jev-off -> createGeneratorOnlyEngine, everything else -> createEngine, jev-only adds opts.synthesizer), runPair provider/decider wiring (runner.ts:504-521), the isRecord shape check (runner.ts:120 via isEngineMode) and the hard-coded prose CONDITIONS_PARAGRAPH (src/bench/report.ts:115-124). The one live jev-on vs jev-off comparison (bench/results/live-swebench-30, Claude Sonnet 5 via OpenRouter, Jev typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917, 25 steps, 20 min, $1.50/run) scored jev-on 9/29 vs jev-off 10/29 paired (9/30 vs 10/29 all records; pytest-10051 jev-off 'invalid'). Cost: jev-on $23.51 generator + $1.55 Jev = $25.06 (Jev is 6.2% of jev-on spend); jev-off $21.19; bench $46.25. Wall: jev-on 5,568 s (mean 3m06s; generator 4,584 s = 82%, Jev 812 s = 14.6%, exec 116 s, harness 52 s) vs jev-off 4,265 s (mean 2m22s). Stop reasons: jev-on max_steps 25 / replan_stop 4 / spend_cap 1 (task cap on sympy-20428); jev-off max_steps 25 / generator_done 5. The run logs show where jev-on wasted budget: 223 of 726 steps (30.7%) never executed (39 blocked + 184 reviews all declined by the bench's alwaysDecline confirmer), every refusal came from the plan_mismatch dimension (0 destructive/out_of_scope refusals), 74 of 104 edit proposals (71%) and 96 of 478 run proposals were refused, 45 refused runs were test invocations (14 plain `pytest -q <file>` forms), the generator never proposed `done` in 726 steps, task_complete peaked at 0.55 against the 0.85 threshold (0 fires in 497 judge calls), intent resolved to `investigate` on 529/726 steps with 90 fallbacks and 41 paired-Noul overrides, 49 loop trips (24 read, 16 intent:unresolved, 8 patch, 1 run) drove 47 replan calls of which 14 had Jev's move overridden by the paired-Noul floor 0.5 (src/loop/stages/choose.ts:10,42-70) and all 4 replan_stop exits were such overrides to stop_and_report at Choice mass 0.02-0.16 (one ended a passing run, django-15572, at step 16), and 13/30 jev-on runs ended with an empty patch (STATUS says 10). Jev's own budget is dominated by the context stage: 726 requests asking 300 Nouls each (208,900 of 220,411 questions, 26.1M of 37.0M input tokens, $1.10 of $1.55, 504 ms mean vs 210-240 ms for other stages, 42 retried requests) to select a mean 1.33 files per step (153 steps selected none). Two measurement defects: (1) 15 of 30 records per condition (the first pass, before commit 271610e landed at 2026-09-19 23:53 -0700 between the first pass 23:03 and the resume 23:55) have zero-filled generatorTokensPerStep/jevTokensPerStep, so comparison.md's split rows (jev-on 5,519 vs jev-off 6,767 generator tokens/step; 28,351 Jev tokens/step) and STATUS's "18% fewer generator tokens per step" are artefacts; true means from steps.jsonl are jev-on 13,991 vs jev-off 12,814 generator tokens/step (+9% for jev-on) and 59,209 Jev tokens/step; (2) every §21.2 risk/loop rule (isVerificationRun, completionVerifiedByRun, novelVerifiedPatch, refused-proposal and fail-set signatures; commits c39e047/382e69f/a030381/42d9f09, 2026-09-20 13:58-16:43 -0700) landed ~17 h after the jev-on bench and applies to jev-on too (src/loop/stages/risk.ts:502-524 is not mode-gated), so the 9/29 number measures an engine that no longer exists and no jev-on bench has been re-run since. No bench result on disk used the new default generator z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (src/config/defaults.ts:7, DECISIONS 2026-09-21); its only live verification is one forced tool call. jev-only finals on the frozen tree: QuixBugs 39/40 ($0.185, 3.54 steps-to-solve, 39 `complete`), ladder 14/20 ($0.32), SWE-bench 4/30 ($1.30, 348 steps, 228 blocked, 88 loops, 61 replans, 20 replan_stop + 7 max_replans, harness time 4,850 of 7,102 s because the synthesizer search is inside harnessMs, 106k Jev tokens/step). The mocked bench (default, no --live) replays goldTrajectory (read touched files -> gold patch -> run tests -> done; src/bench/swebench/loader.ts:65-72) through createMockProvider and answers Jev with createMockDecider's deterministic rules; the mock evaluator is `git apply --check -R gold`; unit tests fake all of BenchDeps including the engines (test/unit/bench/helpers.ts:337-370) so the runner is tested with zero engine code.

decision_points.what: Which conditions run and in what fixed order (CONDITION_ORDER jev-on, jev-off, jev-only); default 'jev-on,jev-off' (src/bench/cli.ts:24). Unknown names are a ConfigError/UsageError.
decision_points.question_shape: n/a (closed string union EngineMode at src/core/types.ts:371)
decision_points.weakness: Adding a condition requires edits in >=7 places: EngineMode union, CONDITION_ORDER, args.ts CONDITIONS, createEngineFor, runPair provider/decider/synth wiring (runner.ts:504-521), isRecord (runner.ts:120 via isEngineMode, else old tasks.jsonl lines are skipped as malformed), CONDITIONS_PARAGRAPH prose (report.ts:115-124), and every engine.ts mode branch (usesJev :364, 'jev-only' :1698/1796/2599, 'jev-off' :1926/2246/2347).

decision_points.what: Every risk verdict 'review' is refused in bench runs (confirm() resolves false; identity 'no reviewer in bench runs'). Counted as declined and folded into `blocked` (runner.ts:224).
decision_points.cost_latency: 184 of 726 jev-on steps (25%) spent a full generator call (~13k tokens, ~6 s) and 3-4 Jev requests to produce nothing.
decision_points.weakness: The bench measures 'Jev + a reviewer who always says no', not Jev; 71% of edit proposals never executed. DESIGN §17/STATUS open question says whether a repeat-of-failed-edit should block or warn is unresolved.

decision_points.what: Per-proposal risk: Jev Scores 4 dimensions (destructive, out_of_scope, plan_mismatch, irreversible, 5 levels) + matches_intent Noul; code turns alignment dims into tail mass P(level>=3) and harm dims into expected level, verdict = ok/review/block by 0.3/0.7.
decision_points.question_shape: 5 questions per request (4 Score + 1 Noul); mean 5,155 input tokens; 723 requests in the live bench
decision_points.cost_latency: 238 ms mean, $0.157 total (10% of Jev cost)
decision_points.weakness: In the live bench 100% of the 223 refusals were plan_mismatch (level 4 'repeats a step recent shows already failed' or level 3 'claims completion while remaining non-empty'), 0 from harm dimensions; 45 refused `run`s were test invocations. Post-bench rule isVerificationRun (risk.ts:215-218) exempts one plain test command (rejects any `;&|<>` composition, so `pytest ... | tail -60` is still refused); 14 of 161 refused runs would now pass it.

decision_points.what: Intent Choice (investigate/edit/verify/fix_environment/finish + none_of_these) with paired can_<option> Nouls; code overrides Jev's argmax when its paired Noul < 0.5 (picks highest paired Noul) and falls back to 'investigate' when none reaches 0.5; a fallback away from the answer feeds the loop detector as 'intent:unresolved' (engine.ts:2333-2335).
decision_points.question_shape: 7 questions (1 Choice + 5 paired Nouls + plan_still_valid); mean 5,312 input tokens
decision_points.weakness: Live: 595 chosen, 90 fallback, 41 overridden; intent was 'investigate' on 529/726 steps (73%), and the risk stage then penalised actions that 'do not carry out intent investigate' (27 refusals cite it). 16 loop trips were intent:unresolved x3.

decision_points.what: After a loop trip, Jev chooses next_move (change_approach/gather_context/fix_environment/revert_changes/stop_and_report) + task_impossible Noul; stop_and_report -> replan_stop, task_impossible >= 0.85 -> impossible; same paired-Noul override applies.
decision_points.weakness: 14 of 47 replan Choices were overridden. All 4 replan_stop exits were overrides: e.g. run 20260920-065605-27bb5pej step 17 Jev chose change_approach at 0.82 (can_change_approach 0.44 < floor) and the code took can_stop_and_report 0.63 -> stopped a run whose patch already passed (django-15572, pass at 16 steps); task_impossible was only 0.10-0.13 in all four.

decision_points.what: Run stops 'complete' when the task_complete Noul >= limits.completeThreshold (0.85 default, recorded in summary.json.conditions).
decision_points.question_shape: judge request: 5 Nouls (succeeded, error_present, new_information, task_complete, task_impossible); mean 5,935 input tokens
decision_points.cost_latency: 224 ms, $0.124, 497 requests (only executed steps are judged)
decision_points.weakness: Never fired in 60 live runs: max task_complete 0.55, per-run max median 0.02. 9 jev-on passes ran to 25 steps with a correct patch on disk; jev-off stopped on its own `done` 5 times. Criteria require a current passing run of the detected test command, which the risk stage was refusing.

decision_points.what: One Noul per candidate file (up to 300, pre-filtered by task mentions/recency/path) asking whether the generator needs it this step; files with p >= 0.5 are inlined into the generator prompt.
decision_points.question_shape: ~288 Nouls per request (300 on repos), mean 35,979 input tokens per request
decision_points.cost_latency: 504 ms mean (3.8 s max), 42 retried requests, $1.097 = 71% of Jev cost, 26.1M of 37.0M Jev input tokens
decision_points.weakness: Yield is 1.33 files per step (max 5; 153 of 726 steps selected 0), and jev-on generator prompts were larger (13,187 vs 12,060 input tokens/call, max 30,473 vs 17,686) while reads dropped only 127 -> 86. The biggest Jev line item buys the least.

decision_points.what: Signatures per step (run:<sha12 cmd>, patch:, read:, done:, intent:unresolved, fail:...; post-bench also `:refused`); 3 identical -> trip -> replan (jev-on) or fixed text (jev-off).
decision_points.cost_latency: jev-on 49 trips -> 47 replan requests; jev-off 29 trips (fixed text)
decision_points.weakness: Refused proposals were counted like executed ones at bench time, so a generator re-proposing a refused read/patch tripped 'read' x3 24 times and 'patch' x3 8 times, feeding replans that then got overridden.

decision_points.where: src/bench/swebench/evaluator.ts (local-venv, steps a-i of DESIGN §13); src/bench/quixbugs/evaluator.ts (run_tests.py); src/bench/ladder/evaluator.ts (pytest tests, tests/ untouched); src/bench/terminalbench/evaluator.ts (reward.json)
decision_points.what: pass/fail per task: SWE-bench FAIL_TO_PASS all in {PASSED,XFAIL} and PASS_TO_PASS in {PASSED,XFAIL,SKIPPED} from the official log parsers; empty model_patch -> pass:false without running; timeout/no results -> pass:null 'invalid'.

decision_points.weakness: Unofficial (no Docker). live-slice-3 lost 4 of 6 verdicts to 'environment build failed: clone/checkout ... failed'; live-swebench-30 lost pytest-10051 jev-off to 'no test results and no sign the suite ran'. Evaluated set differs per condition, so paired n (29) < records (30).

decision_points.what: Bench-wide cap ($60) and per-run cap ($1.50) enforced by one shared meter; a tripped run records stopReason spend_cap and capFired task|bench.
decision_points.weakness: One jev-on run (sympy-20428) hit the $1.50 task cap at step 23 with an empty patch; jev-on per-run cost is 8-15% higher than jev-off so a shared cap censors jev-on first.

decision_points.what: Aggregation: paired = tasks evaluated in every condition minus modelDrift; steps-to-solve over passed only; tokens-per-step curves over runs that reached the step; older records get zero-filled split token series.
decision_points.weakness: Zero-filling is silent: 15/30 records per condition in live-swebench-30 carry zeros in generatorTokensPerStep/jevTokensPerStep while tokensPerStep is intact, so the per-source means and the STATUS 'reading' are wrong (true jev-on 13,991 gen / 59,209 Jev tokens per step; jev-off 12,814).

decision_points.what: Offline decider: first non-escape Choice option gets 0.8, Scores 0.95 at level 0 unless DANGEROUS_COMMAND (rm -rf, sudo, git push --force, curl|sh, mkfs), task_complete 0.95 only when testsCurrent && allPassed && nothing remains (or a `done` claiming nothing remains), context Nouls 0.9 when the file is mentioned in the task or touched this run; every answer passes validateJevResponse; cost = tokens x JEV_INPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN so mocked Jev cost is non-zero ($0.0572 in mock-3).
decision_points.weakness: Mocked jev-on still looped (mock-3: 12 loops / 10 replans over 46 steps, 15.33 steps-to-solve vs 4 for jev-off) because the heuristics do not model completion after the gold patch's test run; mocked pass/fail exercises the pipeline only (comparison.md prints a 'Mocked bench' banner).

reusable_for_llm_jev: Condition plumbing is already generic over EngineMode: to add 'llm-jev' (or a synthesizer-backed 'jev-on') extend the union at src/core/types.ts:371, CONDITION_ORDER src/bench/conditions.ts:12, CONDITIONS src/cli/args.ts:277, conditionConfig (conditions.ts:46-65, decides generatorModel/deciderModel columns), createEngineFor (conditions.ts:114-116), the provider/decider/synthesizer selection in runPair (src/bench/runner.ts:504-521), CONDITIONS_PARAGRAPH (src/bench/report.ts:115-124) and the engine.ts mode branches (usesJev :364; propose dispatch :1796-1808). isRecord (runner.ts:120) and pairedTaskIds (metrics.ts:136) then accept it with no change; summary.json.conditions records the per-condition config verbatim.

BenchDepsWithSynth.createSynthesizer ({decider, redact}) => Synthesizer (src/bench/types.ts:31-33) is the injection point for any propose-stage replacement; EngineOptions.synthesizer is honoured only when mode === 'jev-only' today (engine.ts:1796), so a hybrid condition needs a mode-independent 'propose with synthesizer then/or generator' branch.

Synthesizer contract: synthesize(ctx: SynthesisContext) => Proposal (src/core/types.ts:1067-1071); ctx.ask routes Jev questions through the engine's metered/recorded ask (src/synth/index.ts header), so an LLM-backed synthesizer gets jev.jsonl/decisions.jsonl/meter accounting for free. Generator usage in a jev-only record invalidates it (runner.ts:249-253, JEV_ONLY_GENERATOR_CALLED); a new condition must decide whether that assertion applies.

Offline testing needs no engine: test/unit/bench/helpers.ts createFakeDeps(script: EngineScript) fakes createEngine/createGeneratorOnlyEngine/createMockProvider/createMockDecider/createSpendMeter/createSandbox/createSynthesizer and captures what the runner passed (captured.mockProviders, synthesizerDeciders); the fake live provider already reports model 'z-ai/glm-5.3-flash'. runBenchWithSources(sources, opts, deps) (runner.ts:329) accepts synthetic BenchTaskSource objects (helpers.ts syntheticSource).

MockDecider rules: createMockDecider({rules: [(ctx: {stage, step, state, questions}) => Partial<Record<id, Answer>>], failAt, malformedAt, latencyMs}) (src/jev/mock.ts:239-319; types src/core/types.ts:1461-1477) lets a test script Jev answers per stage/step while unanswered ids fall to the heuristics; answers are validated by validateJevResponse so malformed scripts fail loudly. choiceAnswer/scoreAnswer/noulAnswer builders (mock.ts:54-93) produce wire-valid answers.

MockProvider: createMockProvider({turns: MockTurn[] | (req, i) => MockTurn, model, deltaChunkSize}) (src/provider/mock.ts:33); goldTrajectory(gold, testCmd) (swebench/loader.ts:65-72) and mockTurn(goal, action, plan) (loader.ts:59) build trajectories; quixbugs/ladder loaders build FixAction-based trajectories the same way. The mocked evaluator for SWE-bench is `git apply --check -R <gold>` (loader.ts:101-105); quixbugs/ladder evaluate mocked runs with the real tests.

Per-run transcripts are complete and machine-readable under ~/.jevcode/runs/<runId>/: steps.jsonl (intent, contextFiles, proposal, risk.dims with tailMass/level, outcome.status, judge, completion, decisions[], timing, usage), jev.jsonl (per request: stage, questions, usage, latencyMs, attempts), generator.jsonl (per call: inputTokens, outputTokens, latencyMs, malformed, attempt), decisions.jsonl (every question/answer with verdict chosen/overridden/fallback), transcript.log, model_patch.diff, run.json (config record with sources). tasks.jsonl.runId links a bench record to them.

resolveChoice (src/loop/stages/choose.ts:42-70) and its PAIRED_NOUL_FLOOR=0.5 are the single place where Jev's Choices get overridden; annotateChoiceRows writes 'overridden'/'chosen' verdicts into decisions.jsonl, so override rates per stage are measurable from existing logs (live: intent 41/726, replan 14/47).

Metrics/report are condition-agnostic: computeSuiteMetrics/computeSuiteComparison (metrics.ts:164-190) and renderComparison (report.ts:247) iterate summary.conditionOrder; adding a per-condition row is one entry in metricRows (report.ts:140-159). breakdownSections (report.ts:102-113) already breaks quixbugs by kind and ladder by hunks/difficulty.

Bench --resume (runner.ts:308-318 planPair, :333-348 meter seeding) re-runs setup failures and IN_PROGRESS markers and keeps finished records, so a new condition can be added to an existing bench id and only its pairs run (records for other conditions are kept via `kept`, runner.ts:600-606).

Post-bench loop rules that a fresh jev-on bench would exercise for the first time: isVerificationRun/VERIFICATION_HARM_MAX_LEVEL (risk.ts:204-218), completionVerifiedByRun (risk.ts:232), novelVerifiedPatch (risk.ts:426), verifiedCompletion (engine.ts:2044-2049), repeatedGatherContextExit (engine.ts:2056-2062), refused-proposal signatures and failing-set fail: signatures (loopdetect.ts). None is gated on mode.

docs/STATUS.md:68-101 restates comparison.md numbers (9/29 vs 10/29, 83/124 reads, 208/170, 46/40, 2,631/212,508, 237/547 ms, 5,519/6,767 tokens, 3m05s/2m21s, $22.71/$1.49 vs $20.44) and claims '10 of 30 jev-on runs ended with an empty patch' (tasks.jsonl: 13) and '18% fewer generator tokens per step' (artefact of zero-filled series).
hazards: The headline jev-on 9/29 vs jev-off 10/29 measures an engine that predates every §21.2 risk/loop rule (a030381, 42d9f09, 382e69f, c39e047 landed 2026-09-20 13:58-16:43 -0700; bench ran 2026-09-19 23:03-23:55 -0700). Those rules are not mode-gated (risk.ts:502-524), so current jev-on behaviour is unmeasured; any 'optimise jev-on' work should re-baseline first.

comparison.md and STATUS.md per-source token rows are wrong: 15/30 records per condition have zero-filled generatorTokensPerStep/jevTokensPerStep (runner.ts:157-160 withTokenSeries silently zero-fills pre-271610e records). True: jev-on 13,991 vs jev-off 12,814 generator tokens/step (+9%, not -18%) and 59,209 Jev tokens/step (not 28,351). The combined tokensPerStep series is correct.

Bench reviews are refusals by design (alwaysDecline, conditions.ts:17-23): 184 of 726 jev-on steps were declined and every one of the 223 refusals came from plan_mismatch, none from harm dimensions. Jev-on's pass rate is therefore 'Jev + always-no reviewer', and 71% of edits and 45 test-run attempts never executed; jev-off has no equivalent penalty, so the comparison is structurally biased against jev-on.

Paired-Noul override in resolveChoice (choose.ts:42-70, floor 0.5) discards Jev's argmax move: 14/47 replan Choices and 41/726 intent Choices were overridden; all 4 replan_stop exits were overrides to stop_and_report at Choice mass 0.02-0.16 with task_impossible 0.10-0.13, one of which stopped a run whose patch already passed (django-15572). Runs ended on a code rule the transcript attributes to Jev ('Jev directs').

Completion never fires under jev-on (max task_complete 0.55 vs threshold 0.85 across 497 judge calls) while the risk stage refuses the verification runs the completion criteria require; 9 passing jev-on runs burned the full 25-step budget with a correct patch on disk, inflating steps-to-solve, cost and wall for the condition.

Context stage is 71% of Jev cost and tokens and 2.4x the latency of any other stage (726 requests x 300 Nouls) for 1.33 selected files/step; it also makes jev-on generator prompts larger (max 30,473 vs 17,686 input tokens). Tightening CONTEXT_MAX_CANDIDATES/pre-filter is a pure win the design already lists as open (STATUS 'Open questions').

No bench, live or mocked, has run with the new default generator z-ai/glm-5.3-flash; every result on disk is Claude Sonnet 5 via OpenRouter. The only glm verification is a single forced tool call (234+19 tokens). Its pricing-table fallback is ~1.7x optimistic vs the served provider, so spend caps could be under-enforced when usage.cost is absent. .env.example still documents the Anthropic/Sonnet defaults.

Loop detector counted refused proposals like executed ones at bench time: 24 'read' trips and 8 'patch' trips were the generator re-proposing something Jev had just refused, each trip costing a replan request and often a directive that the risk stage then refused again (pylint-4604: 13 refusals, 2 trips, replan_stop, empty patch). Post-bench `:refused` signatures address this but are unmeasured under jev-on.

Evaluated-set drift: local-venv evaluator infrastructure failures (live-slice-3 lost 4/6 verdicts to clone/checkout failures; live-swebench-30 lost 1) change the paired n per run, and SWE-bench numbers are unofficial (no Docker). jev-only SWE-bench 'passes' are load-sensitive (sympy-19954 flipped across runs) and none has the upstream fix's shape.

jev-only SWE-bench wall is dominated by harnessMs (4,850 of 7,102 s) because the synthesizer's search and shadow-lane test runs are accounted inside 'harness', so the bench's timing split misattributes the synthesizer's cost; a hybrid llm-jev condition would inherit the same accounting unless a 'synth' timing bucket is added.

Adding a condition is a multi-file change with a silent failure mode: a tasks.jsonl line whose condition is not in CONDITION_ORDER is dropped by isRecord (runner.ts:120) with only a log line, and report.ts CONDITIONS_PARAGRAPH is prose that must be edited by hand.

STATUS.md 'reading' paragraph (lines 88-98) carries two wrong numbers ('10 of 30' empty patches is 13; '18% fewer generator tokens per step' is an artefact) and is the text a reader would cite when deciding what Jev is 'really good for'.
